電豎琴具有清澈透亮、如水晶般的音色質感，兼具溫潤柔和的特質。其音域寬廣，從低沉的: The electric harp has a clear, translucent, crystalline timbre that is also warm and soft. Its range is wide, from deep low notes to bright high ones, spanning six or seven octaves. Through an electronic amplification system the vibration of the strings is captured precisely and turned into an electrical signal, producing a clear, penetrating sound. Its resonance is unusual: it keeps the warm body of the traditional harp and adds the sharp definition of an electronic instrument. Compared with the piano its timbre is more transparent; compared with the traditional harp, electronic amplification increases its volume and expressive power, which makes it more competitive in modern line-ups, and it is often used in jazz, new-age music and cross-over work.
電豎琴可見於爵士、藍調、流行、搖滾、拉丁爵士、新世紀與前衛實驗音樂等場合。演奏者: The electric harp appears in jazz, blues, pop, rock, Latin jazz, new-age and avant-garde experimental music. Players go on stage with a solid body or a hollow electro-acoustic body, and can use effects pedals as an electric guitarist does; some small instruments have a strap system so the player can move about the stage. Line-ups include solo playing, duos and quartets, and it has appeared on Björk's albums and tours. It sounds as a chordophone, and its regions cover Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.

The pickups are piezoelectric and fitted at the base of each string, and some electro-acoustic instruments also have a microphone inside the resonator plus a preamplifier. The modern double-strung harp, the gravikord, is mainly of stainless-steel tubing, with a bridge of synthetic material that incorporates piezoelectric sensors. There is also a strap system, but its material is not stated; the materials of the body, the strings and the usual parts are also not stated.
電豎琴是基於原聲豎琴的弦鳴樂器，分實心體與空心體電聲型；實心體無共鳴箱，需擴音，: The electric harp is a chordophone based on the acoustic harp, in solid-body and hollow electro-acoustic types; the solid body has no resonator and needs amplification, while the hollow body can be played acoustically or electronically. Most are plucked instruments, some are pedal harps, and a piezoelectric pickup sits at the base of each string; some have a built-in microphone and preamplifier and can be plugged into a PA and effects units, and small models can be strapped to the body. Its players include jazz-pop, rock-pop, new-age, avant-garde experimental and Latin jazz musicians, and it is used for stage performance.
電豎琴源自聲學豎琴，有實心與空心電聲型號。1950年代末Alan Stivell: The electric harp derives from the acoustic harp, in solid and hollow electro-acoustic models. Alan Stivell had the idea in the late 1950s and designed and built a solid electric harp at the turn of the 1970s and 1980s, at about the same time as Rüdiger Oppermann. He later worked with Joel Garnier, Leo Goas-Straajer and Camac; the first commercially made instrument was built by Camac, and, influenced by Deborah Henson-Conant's requirements, it used a light Celtic-style frame, a piezoelectric pickup for each string and a strap system. At the end of the twentieth century the American musician Robert Grawi created the gravikord on the model of the African kora, using stainless-steel tubing and a synthetic bridge, which makes African polyrhythms easier to play.
電豎琴的演奏以原聲豎琴撥弦為基礎，實心體型因無共鳴箱，必須接擴音系統發聲；小型琴: The electric harp is played by plucking, as the acoustic harp is, but the solid-body type has no resonator and must be plugged into an amplification system to sound; small instruments often have a strap so the harp can be fixed to the body and the player can move on stage. A beginner can start by getting to know the output of the piezoelectric pickup under each string and practising the connection to the amplification; effects pedals work much as they do with an electric guitar. Solid electric harps are mostly plucked, with few pedal models; for unamplified playing choose the electro-acoustic type, which looks close to an acoustic harp and can mix the pickup signal with the built-in microphone.
